sentences.text:
THIS PETITION IS COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
ORDER Petitioners are accused Nos.1 and 2 respectively in Cr.No.56/2023 of Devarajeevanahalli police station registered for offences punishable under Sections 506, 341, 504, 420 r/w 34 of IPC.
2. Petitioners have filed this petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail.

3. Heard the learned Senior counsel for petitioners and the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent-State and perused the material on record.
4.

Complaint allegations are that the accused have induced the complainant to deposit a total sum of Rs.3 Crores with the AKPS Souharada Credit Cooperative Limited wherein petitioner No.1 is the President/Chairman NC: 2023:KHC:21149 and even after the due date, the amount was not paid back.

According to the complainant, the said Society has to repay a total sum of Rs.3,70,00,000/-
(Rupees three crores seventy lakhs only) to him and since he was insisting the accused to pay back the deposit made by him, he was abused, manhandled and threatened etc.
5.
Petitioner No.1 is said to be the Chairman of AKPS Souharada Credit Cooperative Limited wherein the complainant is alleged to have deposited a huge sum of Rs.3,00,00,000/- (Rupees three crores only).
Petitioner No.2 is said to be a person who introduced the complainant to petitioner No.1.
6. Petitioners claim to be innocent and it is contended by the learned Senior counsel that they are falsely implicated at the instance of persons who are inimically disposed.
He would draw the attention of the Court to the observations made by the learned Sessions Judge regarding statement of accounts furnished towards NC: 2023:KHC:21149 the payment of amount.

He has also furnished along with a memo dated 13.06.2023 certain documents including statement of accounts and contended that in fact the amount has been transferred to the account of the complainant.

7. The allegations are that petitioner No.1 being Chairman of the Society and petitioner No.2 who introduced the complainant to petitioner No.1 have committed cheating by not returning the amount deposited by the complainant with the society.

At this stage, the documents furnished by the Sri D Shankar vs State Of Karnataka on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150941854/
2 petitioners cannot be taken into account to hold that the amount has been transferred to the account of the complainant.

sentences.text: The allegations are to be investigated into.

However, in view of the claim of the petitioners that the amount has been transferred, they can be directed to co-operate with the investigation and furnish all the details to the Investigating Officer.
Further, whether there was any intention for the petitioners to cheat the complainant or not is a matter, NC: 2023:KHC:21149 which has to be established during trial.
The offence alleged are not punishable with death or imprisonment of life.
The maximum punishment prescribed is up to seven years.
The learned High Court Government Pleader has submitted that a notice has been issued under Section 41(a) of Cr.P.C., but the petitioners have not participated in the enquiry.
Since the petitioners have failed to respond to the notice, there is a reasonable apprehension of their arrest.
In the facts and circumstances, by imposing necessary conditions, the relief sought by the petitioners can be granted.

Hence, the following:
ORDER i. The petition is allowed.
ii. The petitioners/accused Nos.1 and 2 shall be released on bail in the event of their arrest in Cr.No.56/2023 of Devarajeevanahalli Police Station, Bengaluru City, subject to following conditions:
(1) They shall appear before the I.O. within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a certified copy of the order NC: 2023:KHC:21149 and shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- [Rupees one lakh only] each, with two sureties for the likesum.

(2) They shall furnish proof of their residential address and shall inform the I.O./
Court, if there is any change in address.
(3) They shall co-operate with the  Investigation of the case.
(4) They shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses in any manner.
(5) They shall attend the Court on every date of hearing, without fail.
